references.text: The command to work six days and rest on the seventh day (the Sabbath) is given here as part of the Ten Commandments, confirming the Sabbath principle established with the manna.
Moses explains that the seventh day is a holy Sabbath rest for the Lord, which is why manna does not fall on the Sabbath.
The Lord confirms that He has given Israel the Sabbath and that the people must stay home on the seventh day. This expands on the Sabbath command in verse 26.
Six days shall work be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath, a holy day of rest for the Lord. The same pattern of six working days and rest on the seventh.
Repeats the principle of six working days and Sabbath rest on the seventh day.
The Sabbath is referred to as a holy assembly where no work shall be done, in accordance with the rest on the seventh day.
Moses repeats the Sabbath command in the plains of Moab: six days you shall work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath for the Lord your God.
God rested on the seventh day after creation and made it holy. This is the theological basis for the Sabbath rest mentioned in Exodus 16:26.
The book of Hebrews refers to God's rest on the seventh day and connects this to the spiritual Sabbath rest awaiting God's people.
Links the historical observance of the Sabbath in the wilderness with its establishment as a central commandment.
Explains the historical origin of the Sabbath command and its social purpose.
The verses form an inseparable unit describing the preparation and consequences of the Sabbath law in the wilderness.
